subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Pranav Mehta <pranav@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:10:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Pranav —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture a short recap of the call and next steps so we’re aligned. If I missed anything, please flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain points (as discussed):
- Current spend and unpredictability on OpenAI/Anthropic APIs — token costs are the single largest variable in your infra budget.
- Vendor lock-in and lack of control over model rollout/latency for peak traffic windows.
- Data residency and HIPAA-related concerns for certain PII-containing transcripts — procurement needs stronger controls and auditability.
- Latency spikes for synchronous features in the patient portal during business hours.

Current stack and usage notes:
- Production usage today: OpenAI (gpt-4o) for chat features and Anthropic Claude for another set of batch summarization jobs.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with daily peaks (9am–11am PST and 2pm–4pm PST).
- Authentication: OAuth to vendor APIs, SSO via Okta for internal tools.

Success criteria for migration:
- Achieve comparable quality for top-2 intents (patient Q&A, triage summarization) with model shortlist.
- Maintain or improve 95th percentile latency for portal calls (target <500ms for simple Q&A).
- Reduce per-unit token cost by at least 30% at current traffic levels.
- Satisfy procurement/security checklist items (SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, KMS integration).

Compatibility needs (must-haves):
- API parity for streaming + function/tool calling (we need to integrate with your existing call-flows with minimal app changes).
- Model variants that support quantized deployments and an edge-friendly path for Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache/prefix caching support for long-lived chat sessions.

Initial model shortlist we discussed:
- Llama 2 / Llama 3 family (open weights)
- RedPajama / Together models (server-side variants)
- Mistral / Mosaic (higher-efficiency, good few-shot performance)
- Fallback plan: smaller, pruned open models for cost-sensitive paths (embedding + retrieval combo)

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Marissa: share Redwood migration checklist + security questionnaire (attached) — today.
- Rishi: propose a 2-week POC plan (Dedicated capacity + 1 model variant) and rough cost estimate — by 2026-06-24.
- Pranav: confirm top 2 intents to prioritize and share any redlines from procurement — by 2026-06-22.
- Joint: 30–45 minute technical kickoff with infra and security (Okta/KMS) — target week of 2026-06-29.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx (migration checklist), sso-security-questionnaire.pdf (security questionnaire stub).

Thanks — appreciate the clarity and openness on the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Pranav Mehta <pranav@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, ACME Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap, this looks right. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Top 2 intents to prioritize: patient Q&A and appointment triage summarization. Those drive the most user impact.
- Procurement note: we will need SOC 2 Type II (in-process is okay) and an answers doc for KMS/HSM integration. I looped procurement on this email.
- POC constraints: we can commit to a 2-week POC on non-prod traffic with a 1% sample of production queries. Can you confirm what metrics Redwood will instrument out-of-the-box? (latency percentiles, token counts, model versioning).

Also: cost target is important. If you can show a cost estimate for the sample traffic (current token rate -> Redwood cost), that will help accelerate internal approval.

Happy to do the technical kickoff the week of 6/29. Can Rishi own the POC plan?

Thanks,
Pranav Mehta
Head of Engineering — AI Platforms
ACME Health
pranav@acmehealth.com

Thanks Pranav — I’ll own the POC plan. Quick answers to your questions:
- Out-of-the-box metrics from Redwood Console included in the POC: latency (p50/p95/p99), token counts (prompt/response), per-route cost, model version and rollout metadata, inferred batching stats, and audit logs for requests. We can provide a prebuilt dashboard for the 1% sample.
- For the sample traffic cost estimate: I’ll take your current token-rate and return a side-by-side cost comparison (OpenAI/Anthropic vs Redwood-hosted + Dedicated options) by Thursday (2026-06-24).
- SOC 2: we can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and an architecture note for KMS/HSM integration. I’ve attached the high-level security questionnaire answers to the thread (see attachment).

Proposed POC scope (short):
1) Stand up Dedicated capacity with 1 model variant (we’ll propose Llama 3 small and a pruned Mistral variant).
2) Route 1% sampled production traffic for 2 weeks; instrument metrics + alerting.
3) Evaluate quality on top-2 intents and run automated evals on your prompt set.
4) Provide a cost delta and ops checklist for a staged rollout.

I’ll schedule the kickoff once Pranav confirms timing and procurement provides any additional checklist items.

— Rishi
